topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and environmental versus intrinsic factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational nature of cancer as a multi-step genetic and microenvironmental disease, examining the debate and epidemiological evidence regarding intrinsic bad luck versus environmental exposure.

topics.label: Infectious agents and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, using the discovery and multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: DNA damage mechanisms of physical and chemical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation, dietary toxins, and xenobiotically metabolized chemical compounds induce DNA mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promoters and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, highlighting how chronic inflammation and tumor promoters cooperate with initiators to drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Host developmental susceptibility and summary of carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cellular proliferative state and life stage influence cancer vulnerability, concluding with a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and testing mutagenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Carcinogenic risk-benefit assessment and concluding summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by discussing how individuals and societies weigh the risks and benefits of carcinogenic exposures.
